task: D6.1 manager-authoritative submission detail read path
decision: The existing submission detail URL and page remain unchanged. With MANAGER_UI_DATA_SOURCE=manager, /api/dex/submissions/detail reads one attempt through manager_api at /v1/broadcasts?attemptId=... and maps the manager DTO for the page. It does not call load_cow_execution_attempt_detail or open the business SQLite database. Manager read failure or a missing attempt fails closed instead of falling back to legacy.

implementation.legacyMode: MANAGER_UI_DATA_SOURCE=legacy keeps the existing compatibility detail read and exposes manager_compare=true only as a read-only shadow.
implementation.managerMode: MANAGER_UI_DATA_SOURCE=manager selects manager authority before any SQLite lookup.

managerModeResponse.attempt: page-compatible DTO mapped from manager AttemptRow
managerModeResponse.managerDetail: manager attempt, diagnostics, status versions/checksums, and comparison boundary

fixtures: manager source route returns dataSource=manager without calling the legacy SQLite detail loader
manager source route sends the selected chain id and string attempt id to /v1/broadcasts with limit=1
manager attempt rows map to page-compatible identity, path, status, signed PnL, gas, RPC, receipt, evidence, and timestamp fields
manager diagnostic rows are filtered to the requested attempt id
manager source read failure returns 503 and does not fall back to SQLite
legacy source keeps the existing detail path and only attaches managerShadow when manager_compare=true
manager API HTTP test proves attemptId filtering returns only the requested attempt and its diagnostics
knownBoundary: This evidence covers submission detail only. Summary, category, review, and execution list pages still require their own manager-authoritative DTO mappings before default cutover. The manager attempt id remains a string while legacy page ids are SQLite integers, so production-copy identity continuity must be verified before changing the default data source. No production database migration, service restart, manager write, or broadcast was performed.
